notes.value: Pages 1–6 are one continuous large-scale preparation and workup; reaction photographs Figures 1–4 document appearance/filtration and do not define additional experiments.
The displayed scheme, exact procedure, and Notes 1–11 describe the same main run and are merged rather than duplicated.
Note 11 states that crude 1H NMR showed desired product, THF, and MTBE; this is composition of the crude oil, not a purity or isolated-yield measurement.

GC conditions: DB-1701 column (30 m × 250 um, film 0.15 um), flow 1.2 mL/min, injector 240 °C, 50→150 °C at 15 °C/min, 150→280 °C at 20 °C/min, hold 280 °C for 2 min, FID 280 °C; retention times 2.18 min for propargyl alcohol and 2.55 min for product.

CuI is retained conservatively as a reagent rather than auto-assigned a catalyst role; its source-reported loading is already structured in participant amounts, and the covered procedure does not call it a catalyst.
Note 8 reports white smoke during the portionwise addition and explicitly requires conducting the workup in a fume hood.
Note 10 warns that the pungent reddish-brown residue can clog the filter and instructs decanting only liquid.
Page 7 supplies the source spectra: 1H NMR, 13C NMR, EI-MS, and neat IR for buta-2,3-dien-1-ol; these characterize the existing preparation rather than creating another reaction.

The page-9 discussion summarizes the current 0.4 mol procedure as giving 38–45% product with the source-reported CuI charge already structured in participant amounts; this is a narrative range for the same method, not another run or a replacement for the run-specific 45% outcome.

Page 15 is the crude-allenol 1H NMR spectrum before final distillation. It shows the desired allenol resonances together with peaks explicitly labeled THF; it is characterization of the crude material from the existing procedure, not a new reaction or a purity result.
Page 16 is the 400 MHz 1H NMR spectrum of distilled allenol in CDCl3 and characterizes the already isolated product; it does not define an additional preparation.

Page 17 is the 500 MHz quantitative 1H NMR sample of distilled allenol with the drawn dimethyl fumarate internal standard in CDCl3. The page label abbreviates the standard as DMF, while the drawn structure and the page-7 note identify dimethyl fumarate; no N,N-dimethylformamide participant was created.

Page 18 is the proton-decoupled 125 MHz 13C NMR spectrum of distilled allenol in CDCl3. The 76.74/77.00/77.25 ppm solvent-region cluster overlaps the printed 76.7 ppm product assignment, so no independent peak deconvolution was inferred.

The source does not state whether the page-15--18 spectra were acquired from the 12.5 g main run or the separately reported 12.8 g repeat. They are linked conservatively as characterization of the main reported procedure and are not used to assign purity or spectral outcomes to the second-run record.
